audit_items.proof_trace: CreateList is a plain HashSet instead of JournalSet, so it cannot be restored when CREATE fails. When a CREATE opcode attempts account creation (line EvmState.cs:182), the address is added to CreateList before execution. If CREATE later fails and Restore() is called, all JournalSets are restored (StackAccessTracker.cs:83-87) but CreateList is not, leaving the failed-creation address in the set. This breaks EIP-6780 SELFDESTRUCT semantics which relies on CreateList.Contains() to determine if an account was created in the current transaction.
audit_items.attack_scenario: Attacker submits a transaction that: (1) creates contract A via CREATE, (2) A's constructor calls CREATE2 to deploy contract B but the CREATE2 fails (e.g., insufficient gas for code deposit), (3) attacker later in same transaction deploys a different contract at B's address via normal CREATE2, (4) calls SELFDESTRUCT on B. Because B's address remains in CreateList from the failed attempt, SELFDESTRUCT incorrectly treats it as created-in-same-transaction and allows full deletion, violating EIP-6780 invariant that only actually-created contracts can be self-destructed.
